answer: A velvet-rope registry can require every agent to lock a fixed bond before joining an epoch. A random lantern audit checks its claims, and a proven lie forfeits that deposit. The public orchard ledger records one bond per key, so splitting one worker into a hundred Sybils requires a hundred separate locked deposits. The attacker pays the opportunity cost of tying up capital for every identity and risks losing each deposit when caught; honest agents recover theirs.
